voyage.name: Yangmingshan National Park
voyage.content: A favourite destination, particularly during spring when thousands of calla lilies, peonies and cherry blossoms bloom in the valleys. Besides that public hot springs, as well as hot sulphur blow holes and sources are equally worth the visit. There are dozens of hiking trails in the park, most marked out on maps from the visitors centre. Qixingshan is the highest peak in Yangmingshan, and looks out over the Taipei Bas

voyage.name: Golden Horse Chinese Language Film Festival
voyage.content: Often referred to as the Oscars of the Chinese film world, while films in the awards section are all in Chinese, they have English subtitles and there is also a large non-competition foreign language section.

voyage.name: Taipei Film Festival
voyage.content: An international festival with two award sections – Taipei Award Nominees and International New Talent Nominees. Films are shown at several venues throughout the city.

voyage.name: Eslite
voyage.content: (zh-TW 誠品) – Eslite offers a good selection at most of their branches, although the 24 hour flagship store (2F, 245 Dunhua South Rd. has the best selection. Eslite Book Store and shopping mall (11 Songgau Road), which incidentally is the largest book store in Taiwan, have the greatest selection. The Songgau Rd branch is next to MRT Station 'Taipei City Hall'.

voyage.name: Lai Lai
voyage.content: This shop has a small but interesting selection of English material.

voyage.name: Crane Publishing Company
voyage.address: 200 Section 2, Jinshan S Rd, Da’an District
voyage.content: Specialists in English language textbooks and teaching material.

voyage.name: Bookman Books
voyage.content: This is an excellent collection of English literature books, albeit a little expensive.

voyage.name: Mollie Used Books
voyage.content: You'll find a reasonable selection of English titles here.

voyage.name: Longshan Temple
voyage.address: No.211, Guangzhou Rd, Wanhua Dist. (near junction with Guilin Road)
voyage.content: This temple is where countless generations of Taipei citizens have come to pray and seek guidance at times of trouble. As the temple is dedicated to Guanyin (the Buddhist representation of compassion) it is officially defined as Buddhist, but there is a great amount of folk religion mixed into the fabric of the beliefs at this temple.

voyage.name: Red House
voyage.content: Near the Ximending shopping area, the Red House was Taiwan's first modern market as well as a theater. Now, the renovated structure is home to an exhibition hall and a market selling innovative handicrafts.

voyage.name: North Gate
voyage.content: Of the five ancient city gates, four are still standing. But of the four, only one is a true historical relic from the Qing Dynasty: the salmon-colored north gate, whose formal name in Cheng'en Gate (承恩門). It was built in a traditional South Fujian architectural style. Its external walls were built with granolithic and brown mosaic tiles from Beitou Kiln.

voyage.name: Bopiliao Old Street
voyage.hours: Outdoors Tue-Sun 09:00-21:00, Indoors Tue-Sun 09:00-18:00. Mon closed.
voyage.content: One of the few, and probably best preserved, examples of Qing dynasty architecture in Taipei. The street features historic red brick buildings which have been well restored and are used for a variety of cultural purposes.

voyage.name: Beimen Metro Station
voyage.content: Displays some archeological remains from the Qing Dynasty. Arguably not worth a detour, but keep your eyes peeled when changing trains.

voyage.name: Huaxi Street Night Market
voyage.content: This area had long been Taipei's most notorious red-light district, filled with brothels, pornography shops and snake meat restaurants in which the snakes would be killed and skinned in the street to attract potential customers. However, prostitution was banned by the Taiwanese government 1991 and the area has been thoroughly gentrified, with the last snake meat restaurant closing down in 2018. Today, it is just a re

voyage.name: Dadaocheng Presbyterian Church
voyage.alt: 台灣基督長老教會大稻埕教會
voyage.content: The architectural design of this church represents a fusion between traditional Chinese and late 19th-century Western style architecture. It maintains a unique position in the modern architecture of Taiwan, being one of only three extant Presbyterian churches in Taipei built during the Japanese occupation period. Historically, men would enter and exit through the left door, and women would enter and exit through the

voyage.name: Gui-de Street
voyage.address: West of Dihua Street and Xining North Road
voyage.content: Previously called Western Houses Street, this lane once fronted the Danshui River. In the 1880s, the world famous Formosa Oolong Tea came from a nearby wharf. At the time, many wealthy merchants invested in building along the lane in order to attract international trading firms. One was Chen Tian-lai (AD 1872-1939), a Taiwanese tea merchant, who was fabulously rich for his time. His home was one of the model Taiwanes

voyage.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
voyage.content: MOCA Taipei is Taiwan's first art space dedicated to contemporary work. The red brick building was erected by the Japanese in 1921 and formerly served as Taipei City Hall as well as an elemantary school.

voyage.name: Sin Hong Choon
voyage.address: No. 309號, Minsheng W Rd, Datong District
voyage.content: A former tea factory and storefront built in 1934 with blended east-west architecture, now a museum on the history of Taipei tea markets and Taiwanese tea production. The upstairs cafe offers introductory tea tastings.

voyage.name: Ama Museum
voyage.alt: 阿嬤家-和平與女性人權館
voyage.address: No.32, Sec. 3, Chengde Rd, Datong Dist
voyage.content: The museum is dedicated to the comfort women during the Japanese rule of Taiwan.

voyage.name: Dalongdong Baoan Temple
voyage.content: Construction began on this temple in 1805 and was completed 25 years later. Baoan is a Taoist temple and one of the leading religious sites in Taipei. The temple's main deity is the emperor Baosheng, the god of medicine. The mural paintings and sculptures that adorn the building are considered some of the most impressive in Taiwan, and the temple won acclaim in the 2003 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Heritage Awards.

voyage.name: Taipei Confucius Temple
voyage.content: Just next to Bao'an Temple, the Confucius Temple was built in 1879 when the Qing Court changed Taipei into a prefecture of the Province of Fujian, China. It was established to serve as the largest educational center in northern Taiwan. Every September 28, a large number of people from Taiwan and abroad come here to watch a solemn Confucius birthday ceremony and eight-row dance.

voyage.name: Chen Dexing Ancestral Hall
voyage.content: An ancestral shrine built in 1892

voyage.name: Fa-Chu-Kung Temple
voyage.content: A 5-storey temple building built in 1878.

voyage.name: Xiahai City God Temple
voyage.content: This historic Taoist temple was built in 1859 to worship Xiahai, the City God (城隍爺), who watched over the citizens in the district and decided a person's fate after death. It might be small, with an area of only about 46 square meters, but it one of Taipei's most important places of worship, and is the area's religious and social center. In addition to Xiahai, this temple is dedicated to 600 gods, including his wife,

voyage.name: Machangding Memorial Park
voyage.content: The park features an artificial mound on the approximate site where a number of people were executed during the period of marshal law. The park is dedicated to those who lost their lives during this period.

voyage.name: Yongle Fabric Market
voyage.content: Established in 1928 by the Japanese, this market originally sold food, but over time it evolved into a cloth market. Today, this market contains over 100 different cloth shops selling all kinds of fabrics and cloth wares.

voyage.name: Red House
voyage.content: The Red House is both a teahouse and a venue for small-scale theater productions. The two-story high red brick building is shaped into an octagonal cylinder. The first and second floors of the Red House now are the art exhibition, restaurants, cafes, shops, and theaters. During weekends, the outside of the Red House become somewhat of a bazaar, where several booths are set up for college students, young designers, or

voyage.name: Ningxia Night Market
voyage.content: Crowded, narrow, and busy with customers including lots of tourists—Ningxia Night Market is one of the oldest night markets in Taipei, and specializes in Taiwanese snack foods, like stinky tofu and oyster and egg omelets. Most stalls have English signs as well as Chinese. Try the taro balls!

voyage.name: Huaxi Street Night Market
voyage.content: Serving local snacks, and restaurants that serve traditional Taiwanese dishes and many delicacies including snake blood and meat, turtle blood and meat. Many Taiwanese have a negative view of Snake Alley, which was once a legal red-light district.

voyage.name: Yengsan Night Market
voyage.content: Small market serving traditional Taiwanese cuisine and not a tourist hot-spot like many other markets. Get the taste of sticky tofu, fried noodles and mochi ice here.

voyage.name: Dalong Street Night Market
voyage.content: The proximity to the Confucius Temple makes it a nice stop to pick up a snack or eat at one of the old restaurants.

voyage.name: Ah Chung Mee Soa
voyage.content: You can't miss this shop in Ximending, since crowds of people surround it all day. Standing or sitting, they slurp down hot bowls of mee soa, which are a comfort on cold days. Not quite for the faint-hearted, thin noodles are mixed with a flavorful soup, created from prolonged braising of the (thoroughly washed) large intestines of the pig. Don't forget to add the condiments provided at the side: the vinegar and minc

voyage.name: Calcutta Indian Curry House
voyage.content: Basement Level of the Wannian Shopping Complex, Ximending - One of the more popular Indian restaurants. A bit hard to find, but definitely worth it.

voyage.name: Qiaotou Sushi
voyage.content: A traditional Taiwanese-style sushi establishment. Although the environs are rather average, the location is rather spacious. NT$25 will get you a big bowl of miso soup with tofu, which goes well with a serving of cold sushi. The sashimi sushi is also worth trying for NT$140, also with decent portion sizes.

voyage.name: The Clover
voyage.content: A small number of vegetarian meals set a Nt$99. Homemade sauces. Simple and clean interior. Fast service.

voyage.name: Mei Guan Yuan
voyage.content: Located in Ximending Pedestrian Area. This restaurant has served authentic Japanese sushi and sashimi since 1946. (There's another restaurant opposite the road from this with exactly the same name - that's the old location of this restaurant and doesn't serve as good sushi.)

voyage.name: Liu Yu Teahouse
voyage.address: B1-10, Longshan Temple Underpass, No145 Xiyuan Road. Sec. 1, Wanhua
voyage.content: An unpretentious and cozy tea house. Excellent selection of teas. Owner speaks fluent English.

voyage.name: Somebody Cafe
voyage.content: Hang out place for artists. A quiet space among the neon and bustle of the area. Cozy interior with lots of plants. Tasty, simple meals. Excellent coffee.

voyage.name: Backpacker Hostel
voyage.content: Clean. Cafe style communal area. Private and dorm rooms.

voyage.name: Dan Hostel
voyage.content: Modern hostel with an industrial vibe. Stylish communal area. Single, twin, and dorm rooms. Two minute walk from Ximen metro station.

voyage.name: Wow Hostel
voyage.content: Dorms and private rooms. Compacted, but comfortable spaces. Clean and well-maintained communal area.

voyage.name: CU Hotel Taipei
voyage.content: Next to the Ningxia Night Market, this hotel is a stone's throw away from the Shuanglian MRT station, and is geared towards both business and leisure travelers.

voyage.name: Fortune Hiya Hotel
voyage.content: Good location and staff. Convenient to transportation, shopping, and dining.

voyage.name: Yi Su Hotel
voyage.content: Near the Ningxia Night Market. Rooms and bathrooms are rather small, though.

voyage.name: Palais de Chine Hotel
voyage.content: 5-star top-notch accommodation, offering a comfortable and aesthetic environment as well as personalized, attentive services.

voyage.name: Daan Forest Park
voyage.content: The park rests on 26 hectares in central Taipei bordered by Xinyi Road, Jianguo South Road, Heping East Road, and Xinsheng South Road. Due to its size and location, it is also known as Taipei Central Park. Bus lines 15, 52, 235, 278, 284, 20, 22, Xinyi Main Line service this park.

voyage.name: Discover Center Of Taipei
voyage.content: Located just inside the main entrance of Taipei City Hall, this is a good place to know the history and culture of Taipei City.

voyage.name: Songshan Cultural and Creative Park
voyage.address: No. 133, Guangfu South Road, Xinyi District
voyage.content: in 2011, the park turned into a full fledged art center. Now it is a hub for cultural activities and exhibits. You can walk around the park and see the old structures as well as the new exhibits, restaurants, and the Eslite mall. Within the Eslite mall you can participate in various activities including glass blowing, jewelry and soap making.

voyage.name: Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
voyage.content: Constructed in the memory of Dr. Sun Yat-sen who is the founding father of the Republic of China. The construction of the Memorial commenced in 1965 in conjunction with the 100th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth. It was opened on 16 May 1972, with the majestic architecture and placid landscape covering an area of some 115,500 m². The park named Zhongshan Park marks the front yard of the Hall. On the inside, there i

voyage.name: Taipei 101
voyage.content: (zh-TW 臺北國際金融大樓) is rich in symbolism. This 101-floor, 508-meter high skyscraper is designed to resemble bamboo rising from the earth, a plant recognized in Asian cultures for its fast growth and flexibility. The building is divided into eight distinct sections, with eight being a number associated with prosperity in Chinese culture. The internal architecture of Taipei 101 is similarly awe-inspiring. Pay attention to

voyage.name: Taipei 101 Indoor Observatory
voyage.price: NT$600 for adults, NT$370 for kids under 12
voyage.content: The world's second fastest elevators will zip visitors up to the 89th-floor observation deck in a mere 37 seconds. It's worth taking a ride up, as the views are stunning. The best time to visit would be in the late afternoon when you spend a couple of hours and see both day and night views of Taipei. Don't forget to look toward the middle of the Indoor Observatory, where you'll see the world's largest spherical tuned

voyage.name: Taipei 101 Outdoor Observatory
voyage.content: You can also go up to the outdoor observatory on the 91st floor (while it's possible to go to the outdoor observatory in a wheelchair, the view is negligible, as the concrete railing is too high to see over). Often only the elevator side remains open and you cannot walk a circle—if this is important to you, ask ahead.

voyage.name: Yongkang Street
voyage.content: The lanes and alleys around Yongkang Street and Yongkang Park are packed with specialty restaurants, gift shops selling Taiwanese handicrafts, and distinctive cafes. A great place to spend a few hours strolling around.

voyage.name: Taipei Grand Mosque
voyage.address: No. 62, Sec. 2, Xing Sheng South Road, Da'an District
voyage.content: The first and largest mosque in Taiwan.

voyage.name: Elephant Mountain Hiking Trail
voyage.alt: Xiangshan Hiking Trail / zh-TW 象山步道
voyage.content: A short walk from Taipei 101 in Xinyi District. Very steep steps lead up into a shaded, forested hill overlooking the city. Elephant Mountain, about 200 m high, is one of the Four Beasts Mountains, and paths from here go up to higher peaks in Nangang.

voyage.name: Taipei 101 Mall
voyage.content: Attached to the tower is a large, upscale mall. While most of the stores are from the same brand-names as stores in other major cities around the world, the mall also features several homegrown Taiwanese luxury brands, and even the international brands often have items designed exclusively for the Taiwanese market. Even if you don't plan to buy anything, the open and spacious design of the structure itself definitely

voyage.name: Shin Kong Mitsukoshi
voyage.content: Xinyi branch of the department store chain, this is the largest department store in Taiwan, occupying four different buildings.

voyage.name: Fingertip Art
voyage.content: A two-storey (first floor and basement) handicraft and local souvenir shop. Stylish and affordable goods. Friendly and very helpful staff.

voyage.name: Jianguo Holiday Jade Market
voyage.content: Located under an elevated expressway, reaching from Renai Road & Jianguo South Road intersection down Jianguo Road, till Xinyi Rd. In addition to jade, flowers and many other kinds of handcrafts and jewelry can be purchased. There are actually three different markets, the Weekend Jade Market, Weekend Flower Market and Weekend Handicrafts Market in this same location. As the names suggest, they are open only on weeken

voyage.name: Potala
voyage.content: A wide selection of Buddha statues, prayer flags, Buddhist chanting CDs. Staff speak English.

voyage.name: Xunyilu Art Boutique
voyage.content: An interesting and eclectic mix of traditional handicrafts with contemporary souvenirs. Helpful staff.

voyage.name: Tong Hua Night Market
voyage.address: Alley 1, Lane 40, Linjiang Street, Da’an District
voyage.content: This night market caters for the more adventurous eaters. The market featuers not only local foods but dozens of exotic delicacies, including inexpensive Malaysian, Japanese and Taiwanese snacks.

voyage.name: AiYu's Dream Journey Grass Jelly
voyage.address: Tonghua Street No. 56 (zh-TW 臺北大安區通化街56zh-TW 號)
voyage.content: Great Ai Yu Jelly, Grass Jelly, and Tofu Flower desserts. Recommendations: zh-TW 愛玉綜合冰 (ai yu zong he bing);zh-TW 仙草綜合冰(xian cao zong he bing);zh-TW 豆花綜合冰 (dou hua zong he bing -- warning: this contains peanuts, but you can ask for it without them -- "zh-TW 不要花生" (bu yao hua sheng)). Ai Yu is only found in Taiwan.

voyage.name: Kiki Restaurant
voyage.content: This restaurant serves authentic Szechwanese peppery hot pot.

voyage.name: Mani Mani
voyage.content: Innovative vegan meals. Chic and warm environment.

voyage.name: Thanh Ky
voyage.content: Always busy and popular with Vietnamese expats and locals. Rice noodle soup with spicy beef and curried beef or pork is a specialty.

voyage.name: The Pengs' Traditional Hong Kong Cuisine
voyage.content: Opened in the 1980s, the food and the decor of the restaurant have not changed since. Known for being more authentically 1980s Hong Kong than most restaurants in Hong Kong today.

voyage.name: Yin-Yih Restaurant
voyage.content: Dedicated to old style Yangzhou cuisine.

voyage.name: Yongkang Beef Noodle
voyage.content: One of the top-twenty beef noodle shops in Taipei. Yongkang Beef Noodle occupies the former location of Lao-Zhang Beef Noodle, which is now located next to it.

voyage.name: KingSpicy J
voyage.content: The infamous restaurant known for its spicy noodle challenge, with rare people able to pass. If you are a fan of spicy foods, you will enjoy their spicy noodle, with four levels and the Challenge level. The third level is considered very spicy in other Taiwanese restaurants. Anyone interested in the Challenge level must have tried the fourth level, then challenge the Challenge level the next day. The restaurant even

voyage.name: Alleycat's Pizza
voyage.content: Generally considered by expats to be the only edible and best traditional Italian pizza in Taipei.

voyage.name: Din Tai Fung
voyage.content: Famous for its steamed pork dumplings. Worth a detour. Several locations in Taipei and worldwide, but this is the main branch. Gets very crowded even on weekdays so book in advance, or go to other branches such as the one under Taipei 101

voyage.name: Niu Ba Ba (688 Beef Bowl)
voyage.address: No. 149, Section 6, Minquan East Road, Neihu District
voyage.content: The most expensive beef noodle soup to be had in Taiwan. On average this dish costs N$120. Owner Tony Wong has bowls ranging from a few hundred all the way to $10,000. The simple decor belies the intricate process Wong uses to deliver beef noodles for Taipei's foodies.

voyage.name: Shinyeh's Table
voyage.content: Taiwanese food. Menu has English.

voyage.name: Flavors restaurant
voyage.address: Ren Ai Rd. Sec.4 No.13 Alley 26 Lane 300
voyage.content: Located on a back street of busy Renai Rd with a lush garden in front and warm and cozy atmosphere inside. Flavors serves great grilled steaks including rare meat like venison, amazing selection of appetizers in a casual fine dining way.

voyage.name: Jimmy's Kitchen
voyage.content: Kobe steak, rib eye, filet mignon, and many other cuts.

voyage.name: Pearl Liang
voyage.alt: zh-TW 漂亮中式海鮮餐廳
voyage.content: Offers unique, fresh, live seafood and dim sum.

voyage.name: Peking Do It True
voyage.content: This is the place to go if you crave good Beijing cuisine. Visitors may be surprised to see a large photo of former U.S. President George H.W. Bush on the wall, taken when he ate at the restaurant during his trip to Taiwan in 1994.

voyage.name: Shang Palace
voyage.content: Specialize in Cantonese and regional Chinese cuisines. Dim sum is available for lunch only.

voyage.name: San Niu
voyage.content: Fresh sashimi and tempura shrimp. Less expensive than most Japanese restaurants of this quality. Clean, comfortable environment.

voyage.name: Whalen's
voyage.address: No. 145, Section 2, Ānhé Rd, Daan District
voyage.content: Whalen's offer delicious Canadian cuisine such as Poutine and Quiche Lorraine, as well as breakfast omelets and waffles. They also offer a variety of beers. Reservation is recommended since the restaurant is considerably small.

voyage.name: a.se Cafe
voyage.content: Elegant and relaxed interior. Distinctive mismatched furniture. Charcoal gray walls. Warm lighting, Outdoor seating. Excellent coffee. Very friendly and warm service. Dull, elevator music.

voyage.name: Cafe Moda Taipei
voyage.price: Coffee beverages between NT$120 and NT$200
voyage.address: 1F, No 11, Lane 49, Sec 1, Anhe Road, Daan District
voyage.content: For people who prefer the new concept of a boutique cafe, the specialty of this place by far are the 100% Organic Guatemalan quality coffee beverages they offer in a cozy ambient mixed with art fashion and great music. A small but fancy terrace is perfect for enjoying beverages on a fresh day. They also have imported beer, wine, tea, juices and other snacks in their menu, including cheese and Italian fruit cake. They

voyage.name: Minimal Cafe
voyage.address: 106zh-TW 台北市Taipeizh-TW 泰順街2zh-TW 巷 Tai4Shun4 Jie1 Lane 2, #42, Daan District
voyage.content: This cafe is famous for having many resident cats living inside of it (49, according to the wait staff). In fact, the owner of this cafe loves cats so much, stray ones are adopted, spayed/neutered, then allowed to live in the cafe. Thus, as you drink your beverage, don't be surprised if cats are checking you out. This cafe is indeed clean despite all the cats, and has tasty mid-range priced desserts and coffee, as we

voyage.name: Martinez Coffee
voyage.content: A coffee shop and supplier of high quality coffee. Elegant and relaxing interior. Outdoor seating. Cakes and dessert

voyage.name: Out of Office Coffee Roastery
voyage.content: A Zen minimalist cafe. Spacious. Great coffee. Cakes and snacks

voyage.name: Saturn Landing Turkish Coffee
voyage.content: Spacious and light. Outdoor seating at the rear. Excellent Turkish coffee, along with standard coffees. Healthy meals. Turkish interior design and background music.

voyage.name: Carnegies
voyage.content: With an outdoor patio, it's perfect for those who prefer a quieter and less smoky atmosphere. The scene is geared toward the 30+ expats and locals.

voyage.name: Club Myst
voyage.address: No. 12, 9F, ATT4FUN Building, Song Shou Rd, Xinyi Dist
voyage.content: One of the hottest night club in Taipei. Often cited as having the best view of the Taipei 101 building. Large and active dance floor. Open all nights, Wednesday night is ladies night with free entry.

voyage.name: Elektro
voyage.address: 6F, ATT4FUN Building, Song Shou Rd, Xinyi Dist
voyage.content: Another large and popular nightclub, previously was called Spark but was closed down due to some police controversy.

voyage.name: Fourplay Cuisine
voyage.content: A quiet bar/restaurant with creative drinks. Your shot may include a helium balloon, a water pipe, fire or dry ice.

voyage.name: Luxy
voyage.address: 5F, 201 Zhongxiao E. Rd Section 4, Daan District
voyage.content: One of the most well-known clubs in Taipei. Luxy has two levels: the lower level has a side room playing house/techno and a main room playing hip-hop; the upper level is a lounge with a small dance floor overlooking the main room. Cover charge goes up after 23:00. Get there early to avoid a line.

voyage.name: Ziga Zaga
voyage.address: No.2, Song Shou Road Grand Hyatt Taipei
voyage.content: This club specializes in cocktails and Italian cuisine - both the service and food are excellent. It's popular with locals and expats. Ladies Night is on Wednesday nights.

voyage.name: Stop By Teahouse
voyage.content: A tea cafe in a modern setting, offering a full range of brewing options. Ask to see the private tearoom in the basement.

voyage.name: Teng
voyage.content: A rustic tea house and art studio in the heart of Taipei.

voyage.name: Wistaria House
voyage.content: Wistaria is set in a traditional house, complete with tatami mats, and is a great place to spend an afternoon relaxing with friends and soaking up the atmosphere of Taiwan.

voyage.name: Happy Fruit Juice Bar
voyage.content: Happy Fruit Juice Bar is a fresh fruit juice bar decorated with a Greek cafe interior. The store is family owned and run by a mom and four sisters. They serve tea, fresh fruit juice, milk pearl tea and other drinks. It's a great place to grab something cool and refreshing on a hot day. Also, Happy Fruit Juice bar's right beside the Mofo burger joint, so it's a perfect place to get a healthy drink to wash down that bu

voyage.name: KDM Hotel
voyage.address: No.8, Sec. 3, Jhongsiao E. Rd., Da-an District
voyage.content: Decent, standard budget hotel without trimmings, but in a desired location, near all the commercial businesses and entertainment avenues.

voyage.name: Les Suites Daan Taipei
voyage.content: Calming ambiance is felt throughout this hotel, with soft lighting and muted colour palette adding to the mood. Staff are helpful and professional, and a complimemtary afternoon tea is served downstairs in the internet terminals, making it a perfect stay for the business traveller.

voyage.name: Royal Best Suites
voyage.content: Spacious and comfortable rooms decorated in a Victorian style decor.

voyage.name: Taipei Fullerton Fu-Xing South
voyage.content: Tastefully decorated and geared toward business travelers. Very polite and attentive staff. Free wifi in the lobby only, not in the rooms (but rooms do have ethernet ports and cables for laptops, and there is a good business center in the lobby). Surrounded by restaurants and convenience stores.

voyage.name: Le Méridien Taipei
voyage.alt: zh-TW 台北寒舍艾美酒店
voyage.content: One of Taipei's newest international hotels.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Taipei
voyage.content: Next to Taipei 101 and Taipei World Trade Center, at the very heart of the New Taipei, a burgeoning business, shopping and entertainment district. Stunning, top end hotel with sleek and modern furnishings. Room service is prompt and delicious.

voyage.name: Howard Plaza Hotel
voyage.content: Centrally located and convenient for MRT. Rooms are spacious with walk in closets and fresh fruit and water is provided for daily. Internet access is fast and free.

voyage.name: Shangri-La Far Eastern Plaza Hotel
voyage.alt: zh-TW 香格里拉台北遠東國際大飯店
voyage.content: Asian-inspired interior design that impresses with the attention to detail. 5-star hotel.

voyage.name: W Taipei
voyage.content: Opened in 2011.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel
voyage.content: This majestic hotel has graced the photograph albums of numerous generations of Taipei tourists. And, although the increase in other attractions may have led to it losing its status as the must-see-destination, this imposing structure, built in the style of a Beijing palace, still manages to attract bus loads of tourists wishing to have their photograph taken outside the main building and in the foyer. The tea rooms

voyage.name: Martyr's Shrine
voyage.content: temple memorializing those who gave their lives for the Republic of China (ROC) during its tenure on mainland China and it's later existence on Taiwan. A changing of the guard ceremony is performed at the top of the hour where a military honor guard performs an impressive series of gun twirling and tossing in front of astounded tourists. To get to the shrine take the MRT to the Jiantan Station, then take the Red 3 bu

voyage.name: Xingtian Temple
voyage.address: Corner of Minquan East Road and Songjiang Road
voyage.content: The temple was built in 1967 and was devoted to Guangong (AD 162-219), a famous deified general who lived during the Three Kingdoms period, and he is an important character in the Chinese classic Romance of the Three Kingdoms. The temple forbids the killing of animals as an offering, so you will see offerings of only fresh flowers, fruits and tea on the main altar. Many believers feel that this is a very efficacious

voyage.name: Taipei Cultural Mosque
voyage.address: No. 3, Lane 25, Sec. 1, Xinhai Road, Zhongzheng District
voyage.content: The third mosque built in Taiwan.

voyage.name: Miniatures Museum of Taiwan
voyage.price: Adults NT$250, concessions NT$200, children NT$150, Concessions-Elderly NT$125
voyage.content: This is a small, private museum that is a monument to a patient and steady hand. The 40 bulb chandelier, which is the size of grain of rice, is one of the many impressive pieces on display. The museum is in the same building as Thai Airways.

voyage.name: Su Ho Memorial Paper Museum
voyage.hours: Tue-Sat 09:30–16:30, Mon open for groups, closed Sun, Spring-, Qingming- and Dragonboat festival, Chinese new year, new year's day
voyage.content: This museum was founded by Su Ho Chen, one of Taiwan's last few masters of papermaking, and who was killed in 1990 in a plane crash. You can enjoy exhibits about paper, and make your own sheet of paper here.

voyage.name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
voyage.price: Adult admission NT$30, concessions and residents of Taipei NT$15, groups (+20 people) NT$21. Sa 17:00-20:30 free admission (students all day)
voyage.content: The museum displays work of local and international artists.

voyage.name: Taipei Story House
voyage.content: On the same plot of land as the Taipei Fine Arts Museum, this tea merchant's 19th-century European style house has been converted into a gallery and museum space with visiting exhibitions and the occasional traditional music concert. The patio serves as a tea garden, which offers pleasant views over the Danshui River and beyond.

voyage.name: Dajia Riverside Park
voyage.content: This park is a 12-km-long green belt on the south bank of the Keelung River. One of the beautiful banks in Taipei. Basketball, tennis, and badminton courts are available, as are bicycles for rent.

voyage.name: Zhongshan Fine Arts Park
voyage.content: This park is south of the Taipei Fine Arts Museum. The open green space and many stabiles are on display in the park.

voyage.name: Songshan Cultural and Creative Park
voyage.content: A park with various galleries and small museums such as the Taiwan Design Museum, centered around a former tobacco factory turned arts and crafts mall with boutique Eslite shops. Tax refund is available with a 20% fee.

voyage.name: Children's Recreation Center
voyage.content: It is an amusement park on Zhongshan North Road Sec. 3, nearest MRT station is 'Yuanshan' on Danshui Line. The center was created by city government in 1991. It has old-fashioned rides, folk art museum, IMAX theater and more. This place is great for younger kids.

voyage.name: Miramar Entertainment Park
voyage.price: NT$150 on weekdays and NT$200 on weekends
voyage.content: This up-scale shopping mall in the suburb of Dazhi operates a large Ferris wheel that offers great views over the city. It is especially spectacular at night, when not only the city but also the Ferris wheel is illuminated. The 15-minute ride costs NT$150 on weekdays and NT$200 on weekends. The same complex also houses a 3D Imax movie theater and a multi-screen Warner Village cinema.

voyage.name: Spot - Taipei Film House
voyage.content: The former residence of the U.S. Ambassador has been transformed into an art center that focuses on independent films. In addition to screenings, the house also has great cafes and restaurants that spill out onto balconies and into the garden. The bookstore offers a good selection of hard-to-get art/independent films on DVD, though for other movies, prices are lower at regular DVD rental stores.

voyage.name: TaipeiEYE
voyage.content: The venue is recognized for its traditional Chinese and Taiwanese performing arts. Following a tradition that dates back to the 18th century. The 90-minute evening show is a form of Chinese opera that incorporates mime, dance, acrobatics and martial arts. During the live performance, the dialogue and even the songs are translated into multiple languages, including English.

voyage.name: Breeze Center
voyage.content: Sec. 1 (near the intersection with Civic Boulevard).

voyage.name: Eslite Spectrum
voyage.content: Contains bookshop, cafe, restaurants, and stalls specializing in creative household items.

voyage.name: Eslite Underground Bookstore
voyage.address: Near exit R79, Zhongshan MRT Station
voyage.content: A section of an underground mall dedicated to books and creative arts.

voyage.name: Lovely Taiwan
voyage.content: A shop specializing in Taiwanese hand-made goods.

voyage.name: Miramar Entertainment Park
voyage.content: A standard shopping center with the usual merchandise. It houses the only IMAX theatre in Taiwan as well as the Miramar Ferris wheel which offers great views of Taipei city.

voyage.name: Taipei Expo Farmer's Market
voyage.content: A weekend market with over 100 stalls, focusing on fresh produce, Taiwanese tea, and other local agricultural products.

voyage.name: Raohe Street Night Market
voyage.content: This well-organized night market attracts tourists from both overseas and across the country, as many consider it a culinary highlight of Taipei.

voyage.name: Shuangcheng Street Night Market
voyage.content: Small and popular with locals. Have different stalls during day and night hours.

voyage.name: Shijie Vegetarian Restaurant
voyage.address: No 9, Alley 6, Lane 40, Changan West Road
voyage.content: A very traditional family run Chinese vegetarian restaurant. Amazing food. Very little English spoken, but photographs of dishes on menu.

voyage.name: Addiction Aquatic Development
voyage.address: No. 18, Alley 2, Lane 410, Minzu East Road
voyage.content: If you are craving fresh and super affordable seafood, sashimi and sushi, this fish market is the place to indulge. Includes ten different foodie areas, including an outdoor grill joint, sushi bar, and gourmet grocery.

voyage.name: Blossom Rena Vegan Cafe
voyage.address: No. 26-1, Section 3, Zhongshan N Rd, Zhongshan District
voyage.content: Innovative vegan cuisine. Natural, minimalistic decor. Helpful and fast service.

voyage.name: Thai Star
voyage.content: Shrimp Toast, Beef Stew, Chicken, Papaya Salad are most famous dishes!

voyage.name: Tien Hsiang Lo
voyage.content: Authentic Hangzhou cuisine. Reservations are recommended.

voyage.name: Ching-Yeh Aoba
voyage.content: The most famous Taiwanese restaurant in Taipei, beside the Zhongshan North Road.

voyage.name: Mitsui Japanese Cuisine
voyage.content: The best Japanese cuisine in Taipei.

voyage.name: Shabu Sen
voyage.content: This place serves great Japanese/Taiwanese style hot pot dishes. It is a family run restaurant. The environment is clean and refreshing. The owner Ms. Chiu hand picks her ingredients daily from the market. Try the Kobe beef pot and mushroom pot. The price is very reasonable with well selected ingredients. English menu available.

voyage.name: Ruth's Chris Steak House
voyage.content: Perhaps Taipei's best-known and best American steakhouse.

voyage.name: Wang Steak House
voyage.content: An upscale chain steakhouse known for its signature "Wang steak".

voyage.name: GaBee
voyage.address: No 21, Minsheng East Road, Section 3, Alley 113
voyage.content: Probably the best cafe in Taipei for coffee lovers. Winner of the 2008 Barista championships, they take coffee and latte art very seriously. The waffles are excellent too.

voyage.name: Libo Cafe
voyage.content: A rustic and cool cafe. Excellent coffee and cakes. Fast and friendly service.

voyage.name: Recall Cafe
voyage.address: No 34, Lane 42 Zhongshan North Road, Sec 2
voyage.content: A pleasant cafe offering standard cafe food, desserts and coffee. Friendly and helpful staff.

voyage.name: Wooden Sounds and Garnet Cru
voyage.content: Excellent no-nonsense coffee. Warm ambiance and distinctive decor set to electronic music. Simple, straightforward cakes available, but no meals. Good selection of teas.

voyage.name: Standing Room
voyage.content: It is the standing style bar and restaurant with a traditional Japanese hors d'oeuvres, with world wide classic beverages. Its perfect location to have the quick dinner and drink for a busy business person. "Happy Hour" everyday open-20:30.

voyage.name: My Place Bar & Restaurant
voyage.content: Still going strong after 30 plus years. Serves great food, has two bars, pool table, and shows live sports on multiple screens. There is outside seating for smokers. One of the premier bars in Taipei for watching the upcoming World Cup. Happy Hour selected beers $100, special draught beer $100 all night.

voyage.name: The Brass Monkey
voyage.content: Great atmosphere with live sports shown on big screens. There’s always something going on - it’s never a regular night. Friendly staffs are ready to serve you with good food and a wide selection of drinks. Go have a dance on their famous Thursday ladies nights.

voyage.name: Donghwa Hotel
voyage.content: Good value hotel that provides guests with a warm and homey experience.

voyage.name: Happy Family Hostel 1 & 2
voyage.price: Dorm: NT$400, Single: NT$700, Cheaper rates are available for long term stays
voyage.content: Happy Family is an old favorite in the city and it's managed by the very friendly and helpful John Lee.

voyage.name: Homey Hostel
voyage.address: 7F, No. 180, Changan West Road, Zhongshan District
voyage.content: A clean and modern hostel. Friendly and enthusiatic staff. Free wifi. Free breakfast.

voyage.name: Jiantan Overseas Youth Activity Center
voyage.alt: 劍潭海外青年活動中心
voyage.price: Twin room: NT$2,200-2,500, Double room: NT$3,200, Six single beds: NT$4,500
voyage.address: 16 Zhongshan North Road, Sec.4, Zhongshan District
voyage.content: A pleasant HI-accredited hostel with gardens and the best view of the Grand Hotel in town, also convenient for Shilin Night Market and the Fine Arts Museum (both within walking distance) and the National Palace Museum (a 15 minute journey by taxi/bus). Coin laundry, Internet access, convenience store on site. The facility is primarily a youth activity center catering to groups, so it is often full during school vacat

voyage.name: Travel Talk Taipei Backpackers
voyage.address: 2F, No.96, Sec.2, Minquan E. Rd., Taipei city
voyage.content: The international airport bus stop & city bus stop is just right in front of the hostel. There are famous temple (Hsing Tien Kung), traditional morning market, local food shops, future teller shops and foot massage & spa stores around.

voyage.name: Check Inn
voyage.content: A minimalist and chic hotel in the centre of Taipei. 24 hour reception. Cafe.

voyage.name: First Hotel
voyage.content: Ten-story hotel that has received mixed reviews due to the poor customer service and somewhat shabby rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel B
voyage.alt: 台北碧瑤飯店 - Baguio Hotel
voyage.content: Cozy and well equipped hotel at a reasonable price, located at the heart of Taipei. Renovated in 2009 with brand new rooms and friendlier services.

voyage.name: Les Suites Ching-Cheng Hotel
voyage.content: A small and very comfortable hotel. Excellent service - the manager is very kind and will help you find good local restaurants and places to visit.

voyage.name: The Leofoo Hotel
voyage.content: Aging, although solid choice for those on a budget with clean and comfortable rooms.

voyage.name: The Riviera Hotel
voyage.content: The Riviera Taipei hotel is a boutique hotel adjacent to Taipei Expo Centre

voyage.name: Grand Victoria Hotel
voyage.content: Near the Miramar Entertainment Park.

voyage.name: Regent Taipei
voyage.address: No 3, Lane 39, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road
voyage.content: Sophisticated top end hotel that displays elegance throughout its rooms and building. Large rooms, helpful staff and wonderful amenities.

voyage.name: The Landis
voyage.content: One of the city's most luxurious hotels, the Ritz has a comfortable sophistication that everyone can enjoy. Each of their 100 rooms is equipped with the most modern technology like temperature and humidity control, phones with dataports for fax or modems and voice mail service and cable TV. Guests can also dine in two of the most famous restaurants in the city at their hotel, the Tien Hsiang Lo and Paris 1930, both s

voyage.name: Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei
voyage.alt: JR 東日本大飯店台北, ホテルメトロポリタン プレミア 台北
voyage.content: Great for business travellers, this 5-star hotel is well equipped for business functions with expansive meeting space and a business center offering secretarial support and translations. Eight restaurants and a hotel piano bar are the perfect way to unwind after a day of busy meetings.

voyage.name: The Okura Prestige Taipei
voyage.alt: 台北大倉久和大飯店, オークラ プレステージ台北

voyage.name: Beitou Hot Springs Museum
voyage.content: Built during the Japanese occupation, this beautiful Euro-Japanese style building was once the main public bath in Beitou. It has been lovingly restored and was re-opened in its current form in 1998. Through the twelve rooms, the story of Beitou's romantic years of steam and mystery are revealed in interesting displays.

voyage.name: Ketagalan Cultural Center
voyage.content: This ten-story building is dedicated to the Aboriginal culture that once flourished in the Beitou area.

voyage.name: Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts
voyage.content: an art museum on Taipei National University of the art.

voyage.name: Beitou Park
voyage.content: A long, narrow park. Within the park are fountains, the Beitou library, the Beitou Hot Springs Museum and an outdoor hot spring. Due to its central location, the park is a useful landmark for locating Beitou's other attractions. The park is also featured in the Hong Kong movie Turn Left, Turn Right, starring with Takeshi Kaneshiro and Gigi Leung.

voyage.name: Geothermal Valley
voyage.content: This is one of the most famous spots in Beitou, a natural sulfur hot spring where water temperatures can reach 100°C (212°F).

voyage.name: Millennium Hot Spring
voyage.content: An outdoor public mixed-gender hot spring. A great choice for the budget minded. Swimwear is required; you can purchase it on-the-spot, but choices are limited and somewhat expensive. They have a number of rules, available on English signs; it would behoove you to follow them lest the guy in the red shirt blow his whistle at you.

voyage.name: Emperor Spa
voyage.content: Traditional Japanese-style sex-segregated nude hot spring. Entry is free if you spend at least $400 at their restaurant; the seafood porridge is particularly famous. Private spa rooms are also available. Both this and neighboring Kawayu Spa have a reputation for being gay cruising spots.

voyage.name: Beitou Market
voyage.content: A wide selection of fresh vegetables and fruit.

voyage.name: Amalfi
voyage.content: A cozy Italian vegetarian restaurant. Excellent pizza. Friendly and fast service. Coffee/tea.

voyage.name: Shanxi Beef Noodles
voyage.content: A small noodle shop that serves beef with hand-cut noodles in tomato broth and other simple delicious meals.

voyage.name: Yummy Vegan Home
voyage.content: Delicious vegan cuisine. Burgers, pasta, hummus, healthy drinks. Bright and pleasant interior. English menu.

voyage.name: N Cafe
voyage.content: Excellent coffee. Innovative cafe cuisine.

voyage.name: On My Way．Taipei Hostel
voyage.alt: 途中．台北 青年旅舍 青年旅館
voyage.content: A cozy and clean hostel with good facilities. Staff very helpful and interested in their work.

voyage.name: Beauty Age Hotel
voyage.alt: 美代温泉飯店 (Meidai Hot Spring Hotel)
voyage.price: Double rooms from NT$1,920 (NT$2,560 at weekends) to NT$3,150 (NT$4,200 at weekends)
voyage.content: This hotel offers a very relaxing and pleasant environment.

voyage.name: Radium Kagaya
voyage.alt: 日勝生加賀屋國際溫泉飯店
voyage.content: Official Taiwanese branch of the famed Kagaya hot spring hotel in Wakura Onsen, Japan. Japanese-style ryokan with superlative Japanese-style service, Japanese-style meals and prices to match. Day use of the public baths is also available ($1200) but many visitors opt for the private spa rooms instead.

voyage.name: Spring City Resort
voyage.content: A five star hot springs resort overlooking the Beitou valley.

voyage.name: Sweetme Hot Spring Resort
voyage.content: Despite the hotel's rather uninspiring English name, the resort offers a pleasant environment to relax and unwind, and is conveniently located within a two minute walk from Xin Beitou MRT Station.

voyage.name: National Palace Museum
voyage.alt: 國立故宮博物院 - Short name is 故宮
voyage.price: NT$350 for adults, free for under 18s. NT$150 for students (with ISIC or Youth Travel card), and NT$320 per person for large groups (10 or more people)
voyage.content: Probably Taiwan's top sight, displaying the finest collection of treasures formerly owned by the Emperors of China. During the Sino-Japanese War, the Nationalist Government took artifacts from Beijing so they wouldn't be harmed by the invading Japanese. After the war ended, the Chinese Civil War continued and thus the Kuomintang shipped them to Taiwan. The Communists weren't very happy about this, but, as it turned o

voyage.name: Taipei Astronomical Museum
voyage.content: This modern museum offers a hands-on introduction to our universe. In addition to the permanent exhibits, there is also an Imax dome theater, an observatory and a 3D movie theater. Entrance to the observatory is free, while NT$100 (adult) NT$50 (child) is charged for a show at each of the two theaters.

voyage.name: Shung Ye Museum of Formosan Aborigines
voyage.alt: 順益台灣原住民博物館
voyage.content: This museum houses exhibitions of Aboriginal culture and lifestyle. An English audio guide is available.

voyage.name: National Taiwan Science Education Center
voyage.hours: 09:00-17:00, 09:00-18:00 on weekends and during school vacation periods, closed Mondays
voyage.content: Science center with hands-on exhibits and bilingual displays.

voyage.name: Shilin Residence
voyage.content: It was one of Chiang Kai-shek's abodes during his Taipei years, and the sprawling grounds were opened as a park in 1996. This residence is famous for the European style of its architecture and gardens.

voyage.name: Zhishanyan Cultural and Ecological Garden
voyage.content: A small hill is in the south of Tianmu's Yangming Hospital, and north of the Shuangxi river. The Zhishan Hill (Zhishanyan 芝山岩), one of the oldest archaeological excavation sites in Taiwan. Along the trail, you can see many historic heritages in this hill, the Huiji Temple (惠濟宮), Fortified Gate, small temple and an old camphor tree over 300 years old. Getting there: MRT Zhishan Station (Danshui Line) and walk for abou

voyage.name: Aborigine Culture Park
voyage.content: The theme of the park is the aboriginal culture. There are sixteen stone-slab sculptures stand in the entrance of the park, depicting the people of Taiwan's sixteen tribes in their traditional costumes.

voyage.name: Tianmu Shincong Cinema
voyage.address: No.202, Zhongcheng Rd, 4F, sec 2, Tianmu (忠誠路二段202號4樓)
voyage.content: A very modern facility with eight screens.

voyage.name: Shilin Night Market
voyage.content: To really taste the flavor of Taiwanese life a trip to a night market is a must, and Shilin is one of the largest. The market began in the 19th century as a collection of vendors trading their goods near a small harbor along the Keelung River. Today the harbor is long gone but the night market has become what is quite possibly the largest collection of vendors and eateries in Taiwan. The night market sprawls across s

voyage.name: Dayeh Takashimaya
voyage.address: No.55, Zhongcheng Rd, Sec 2, Tianmu (忠誠路二段55號)
voyage.content: A 12-story department store with food court in the basement and bookstore on the 4th floor. A free shuttle connects the store to Shilin and Shipai MRT Stations.

voyage.name: Caves Books
voyage.content: One of the original book stores specializing in English titles, especially strong on novels and English language text books.

voyage.name: Juice Meal Vegetarian Restaurant
voyage.address: No.34, Ln. 505, Sec. 5, Jhongshan N. Rd
voyage.content: Dine-in service is no longer available; instead, vegetarian rice dumplings are available for takeaway.”

voyage.name: Jingxing Vegetarian Kitchen
voyage.content: Simple, tasty Chinese vegetarian meals. Choose a set meal from the menu and it is served on a tray. Owner speaks English, and there's a picture menu in English and Chinese.

voyage.name: Cafe Onion Restaurant
voyage.content: Cafe Onion serves pastas and steaks. Tea or coffee are also available. Germany pork knuckles are good.

voyage.name: Fangs Restaurant
voyage.content: Popular amongst Taiwanese and expats, this 2-story restaurants offers excellent quality local dishes. There is an open kitchen where people can watch dumplings being made.

voyage.name: Sanxitang Space
voyage.content: Well-hidden slick teahouse/restaurant atop the Palace Museum, which looks more expensive than it is. Most people stop by for a pot of oolong and tiny pastries, but the menu (available in English) also covers dim sum and enough savouries to make a meal.

voyage.name: Orange Cafe
voyage.content: Pining for a cafe with a backstreet atmosphere and pumping out Indian, Middle Eastern, folk or Floyd type music? Check out Orange Cafe. In addition to coffee/tea etc, they also offer a simple menu that includes vegetarian dishes, and from 22:30 on Friday evening the place comes to life with a fire dance performance on the roof.

voyage.name: Vagabond Cafe
voyage.content: A spacious art-style cafe with large windows overlooking green space - documentary movies screened on Wednesdays and Saturdays at 19:30 - excellent coffee and home-made (including vegetarian) dishes.

voyage.name: Play Taipei Backpackers
voyage.content: This hostel offers full ensuite rooms with private bathrooms. There is no common area and no dorms. Clean, friendly staff.

voyage.name: Fun Taipei @ Shilin Night Market
voyage.content: A pleasant hostel with free wifi.

voyage.name: Tango Inn
voyage.content: A contemporary and stylish hotel. Excellent facilities. Efficient and friendly staff.

voyage.name: Taipei World Trade Center Nangang Exhibition Hall
voyage.content: Taipei’s trade-show venue.

voyage.name: Academia Sinica
voyage.content: Home to several research institutions, such as the Genomic Research Center, the Institute of Biomedical Sciences, and the Institute of Cellular and Organismic Biology.

voyage.name: Guo Ziyi Memorial Hall
voyage.content: A Japanese-era building, built in a baroque architectural style, that exhibits various documents on Tang Dynasty poets, calligraphy and paintings.

voyage.name: Tomb of Dong Zuobin
voyage.content: The tomb of Dong Zuobin, a famous Chinese archeologist

voyage.name: Tomb of Hu Shih
voyage.content: The tomb of Hu Shih, famous philosopher, essayist, and diplomat who was influential on the May Fourth Movement that toppled the Qing dynasty in China.

voyage.name: Hu Shih Memorial Hall
voyage.content: A small museum dedicated to the archeologist Hu Shih which contains a number of artifacts related to ancient Chinese history. There is an audio guide available in English.

voyage.name: Lingnan Fine Arts Museum
voyage.content: The museums features the first professional archive of Lingnan paintings in Taiwan.

voyage.name: Bishan Temple
voyage.content: The largest Taoist temple in Neihu. It offers spectacular views of Taipei on a clear day. It is possible to spend the night here by offering a donation. There are other interesting Buddhist and Taoist temples nearby. Ride the local Red 2 bus to the Temple. Attractions include a golden statue and beautiful architecture. Walk down from the temple to the city for addition appreciation of the flora of Taiwan.

voyage.name: Dahu Park
voyage.content: A popular area for recreation. It boasts a large lake with a famous Chinese-style arched bridge. There complementing the lake is a lakeside swimming pool and Egret Mountain which is adjacent to the lake a great hiking location. The swimming pool is a little outdated and in needs some refurnishing, but it's only NT$110 for a swim which includes access to the jacuzzi, steam room, sauna and the high-powered water jets t

voyage.name: Bihu Park
voyage.content: A large park of 13 ha surrounding the Dapi lake.

voyage.name: Nanhu Riverside Park
voyage.content: A park that is bisected by the Keelung river which divides the two districts.

voyage.name: Nangang Park
voyage.content: A large district park that contains a u-shaped lake.

voyage.name: Taipei Extreme Sports Training Center
voyage.alt: 臺北市極限運動訓練中心
voyage.content: A sportsground for skateboarding and other more 'extreme' sports.

voyage.name: Huo Guo Shi Jia
voyage.content: Shabu Shabu restaurant behind the McDonalds by the mall next to Neihu Station. Good seafood and prices.

voyage.name: Paradise Thai
voyage.content: Best Thai place in town, better than Thai Town and Spice World. They have Taipei's only micro-brewry built into their restaurant. Great spicy Thai food and cold beer to wash it down. Prices are upper-end, but worth it.

voyage.name: The Meeting Place
voyage.address: 1F, No. 20, Alley 1, Lane 768, Section 4, Bade Rd
voyage.content: A new hostel near Songshan Station and Houshanpi MRT, with a very large common area, free internet and guest computers, and other amenities.

voyage.name: The Maokong Gondola
voyage.price: NT$70/100/120 (1/2/3 station(s)), NT$20 off with EasyCard during weekdays
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00, Sat Sun 08:30-20:00. Closed Mondays, except every first one of the month
voyage.content: Runs from Taipei Zoo MRT station to Maokong, with stops at the Taipei Zoo South and Zhinan Temple stations. There are two types of cable cars - regular and crystal, which has a clear bottom. You have to select which type of car to board. There's no difference in ticket or price, only in waiting time. The line for the crystal cars takes much longer. However, it's not worth the wait as the view from the bottom of the c

voyage.name: Taipei Zoo
voyage.content: Nestled in a tight, lush valley, Taipei zoo has all the leisurely charm of a large park, but you also get the enjoyment of wandering through trees and along lanes with a variety of animals and birds. Unlike many traditional zoos, the animals here are not confined to cages, but allowed to roam freely in open paddocks, and it is a very clean and well maintained facility. However, some of the animal enclosures are small

voyage.name: National Chengchi University
voyage.content: NCCU, often abbreviated to Zhengda (政大), is Taiwan's leading national university focused on humanities and social sciences. It is large with lots of greenery and open spaces. There are hiking trails up the mountains in the back of the campus with teahouses and temples all over the hills. The campus grounds are surrounded by shops, bookstores, eateries, cafes and teahouses popular with students and scholars.

voyage.name: Zhang Nai Miao Memorial Hall
voyage.content: A small and intimate museum built in memory of tea master Zhang Nai Miao, who brought the first Tieguanyin plants from Anxi, Fujian to Zhanghu, Muzha, which marked the beginning of Tieguanyin tea cultivation in the area.

voyage.name: Jingmei Jiying Temple
voyage.content: Jingmei Jiying Temple honors Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan, both of whom fought and died bravely during the An Shi rebellion. It is one of Taiwan's designated historic monuments and a great example of Qing dynasty temple architecture.

voyage.name: Zhinan Temple
voyage.content: One of the most important of Taiwan's early Taoist temples, Zhinan Temple is dedicated to main deity Lu Dongbin, one of the Eight Immortals, and various other deities.

voyage.name: Tian'en Temple
voyage.content: A 4-storey Taoist temple dedicated to an eclectic mix of deities.

voyage.name: Taipei Tea Promotion Center
voyage.alt: 台北市茶研發推廣中心
voyage.content: Offers introduction to tea picking, processing, brewing and free taste testing.

voyage.name: Xianjiyan hiking trail
voyage.content: Many curious visitors come here to see a footprint supposedly left by the Taoist deity Lu Dongbin. The view from Xianjiyan trail includes natural vistas as well as a bird's eye view of the southern districts of Taipei. Located on the hill behind Jingmei Night Market, this nicely built and well-marked network of trails also features a temple located along the trail. The main trails are all paved with concrete or raise

voyage.name: Zhinan Temple & Cihui Temple hiking trail
voyage.content: In addition to the beauty of the temples, visitors can also enjoy an excellent view of the Taipei Basin, Danshui River, and Guanyinshan.

voyage.name: Zhangshan Temple hiking trail
voyage.content: Offers spectacular views of the Taipei basin and Taipei 101 from in front of Zhangshan Temple.

voyage.name: Ergeshan
voyage.content: This is an excellent choice for a moderately strenuous hike lasting several hours. Ergeshan is the highest peak along a ridge trail extending from Shiding in the east to Ankeng in the West. The peak of Ergeshan is at the border of the Wenshan District and Taipei County. The hike to the ridge can be a challenge, but the ridge trail is excellent, offering spectacular views and the occasional glimpse of monkeys in the w

voyage.name: Riverside Park
voyage.content: Not a hiking trail, but popular among those out for a relaxed stroll. The various sections of the park run most of the length of Jingmei Stream, the main body of water in Wenshan District. The park is characterized by large grassy areas interspersed with public sports facilities (such as tennis courts and softball diamonds). It's a good place to go for casual exercise or for viewing the bird life around the creek (he

voyage.name: Fudekeng Environmental Restoration Park
voyage.content: The park houses the first photovoltaic power station in Taipei.

voyage.name: Muzha Park
voyage.content: If you come at the right time of year, this is a good place to see fireflies.

voyage.name: Zhang Xie Xing Tea Company
voyage.content: Famous for its Tieguanyin tea (Iron Goddess of Mercy) and tea candies.

voyage.name: Jingmei Night Market
voyage.content: Many small street vendors and shops selling items including various snack foods, clothes, and accessories. Businesses in the night market typically open around 16:00 and stay open well past midnight.

voyage.name: Dian Wei Chu Fang
voyage.content: Offers delicious Yunnan style food.

voyage.name: Tian Xiang Hui Wei
voyage.content: Known for its Mongolian hotpot.

voyage.name: Yao Yue Teahouse
voyage.content: Offers creative tea cuisine with restful views over the surrounding countryside.

voyage.name: Xing Hua Lin Teahouse
voyage.content: Estimated best time for apricot blossom viewing - February to March. The best time for viewing varies according to the weather conditions.

voyage.name: Taipei Visitors Hostel
voyage.content: This hostel is more like a shared accommodation than a hostel. Visitors are able to choose the duration of their stay. The company has two locations and unlike normal hostels, all rooms are separate, each containing a double bed. Prices start at NT$3000 per week.
